P1.evidence: A KFS setter suffix is on the file and the prospect references a prior text thread, but nothing was read back and the rep confirmed the thread was not his. The frame ran the familiar two of four parts. Frame agreement was taken and given ('if that sounds good' / 'Yeah, sounds great'). The open question is notably improved: 'So how can I potentially help?' - which is the exact phrasing the sales manager coached the day before in place of asking for the biggest challenge, so this is visible same-week uptake of coaching.

P2.evidence: Weight was established and confirmed (185, bouncing to 190, down from 240) and age was volunteered; height was never asked, though the prospect referred to a chart 'for my height and age'. Work was covered properly - the shipyard electrical department, the sawmill, the 5:30 to 2:30 schedule and the fact that he sits all day. Nutrition is the standout and the best in the batch: 'How's that going for you? you have a good plan? Do you track macros?' followed through into breakfast, lunch, dinner, portion control, alcohol history, soda and water intake. Training was explored well. The failures are the medical ones. General health conditions were never asked. The injury check produced excellent work on the hips and waist - 'where are you noticing the lack of mobility showing up in your day-to-day?' and 'Does that show up when you're working out as well?' - but the prospect had already disclosed an injury in Iraq, eighteen months of rehab, back surgery and a medical discharge, and not one follow-up question was asked about any of it. Sleep was never asked despite him volunteering that he wakes at 3:30am and starts work at 5, and despite the programme being described later as tracking sleep. Energy was never asked as a baseline.

P3.evidence: The best goals work in the batch on the vertical axis and the worst on the horizontal. The 1-10 scale was run cleanly ('I'd say about in the middle, about a 5') with a follow-up on which areas would move it. The bridge question was asked exactly as scripted - 'help me understand, like, what's going on right now that's making this a priority for you' - and produced the disclosure that he had been divorced the previous Thursday. The follow-through was also correct: 'And how does that connect into the fitness?' produced a genuinely deep answer about training as a productive outlet, confidence, and being able to walk taller. The reflect-back at 00:16:56 was the most accurate of the batch. What is missing is everyone else. He has two young children, a son on a travelling baseball team, and a family business that was being built 'for the four of us' and is now dead. Nobody asked who this impacts or drove through to the kids. The rep asked about dating instead, and got 'this is all for me. It's not for anybody else specifically' - which is the answer you get when you ask about a girlfriend rather than about his children.

P4.evidence: Only partly run, and mostly through the Trevor question rather than as a phase. What he has tried was covered narrowly - a month of following Trevor's free content and a few routines in the last few days - and the prospect supplied the gap himself without being asked: 'for me to try and develop my own routine would be a trial and error that would take me six months. Versus getting coached would give me the knowledge base up front on how to do it right so I inevitably don't hurt myself.' The rep echoed it back well. But the bigger past attempt was never explored at all: this is a man who lost 55 lb and quit drinking on his own eighteen months ago, and nobody asked how he did it, what made it stick, or why the training half never followed. There was no root-cause question and no 'why can't you stick to it on your own'.

P5.evidence: Not run - the sixth consecutive sales call in this batch with the entire 20-point Consequence Frame absent, and the one where the cost of skipping it is most visible. A 50-year-old, five days after a divorce he did not choose, watching the physique and mobility decline, with the family business gone and two kids to stay in shape for. He had already gestured at the alternative himself - 'It was a better outlet than sitting around doing nothing, sulking.' A two-year question, 'is that something you're willing to settle for', and a line in the sand were all available and none were asked. Without them there was nothing weighing against an unknown legal settlement when money came up.

P6.evidence: The best-sequenced commitment work in the batch. Before presenting anything, the rep set a qualification frame - 'the whole reason why we have these calls is just to make sure that, hey, if we invite you into the program, would you have a high likelihood of success?' - and then took a commitment: 'the main thing that really Trevor wants to know is, like, hey, if you were to do this, you know, really, like, how committed are you to actually following through and doing everything he says so that you actually get the results?' The answer was clean: 'I'm definitely committed. There's no doubt about that.' He then correctly moved forward on that yes. What is missing is the belief question - whether the prospect thinks he can actually get there with the right structure - and the all-in question in its scripted form, which is the one that surfaces hidden blockers like an unresolved divorce settlement before the price is spoken rather than after.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and no payment was collected. The onboarding sequence was described in advance - app access, training platform, community and an onboarding form for Trevor - but never reached. No link was sent and no callback was booked; the entire follow-up rests on the prospect texting after his lawyer meeting.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete money play in the batch, and still short of the script. Run correctly: the permission question - 'if you're open to it, we can have a conversation about what maybe you could do and then see if we can come up with something' - which got a yes; an attempt at the financial picture, 'What could you...?'; the isolate, asked in near-scripted form, 'Outside of the money, is there anything else that's coming up for you?'; and a genuine payment structure, a 24-month financing split. Missing: none of the six specific financial picture areas were asked - no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments - and the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame never ran. The rep hit a real wall, because the prospect genuinely cannot know his numbers until the settlement completes, and the honest response to that ('kind of hard for me to come up with a plan if you have no idea') was correct. What was not correct was the suggestion that followed it about paying before the ex-wife could claim half.

Trigger was 'That I'm going to have to think of', immediately qualified as money. Isolating it to finances was the right first move and the rep made it. But the objection was later re-tested only in money terms, and none of the OA moves ran - no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you there', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no decision-identity move. In fairness the deferral here is substantively real rather than a stall, which is why this scores partial rather than miss.

Trigger was the deferral to the legal timeline: 'gotta go talk to my lawyer to figure out what the bottom line is.' No scripted move ran - no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', and in particular no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', which is the move built for a 50-year-old already watching his mobility go. The rep accepted the lawyer's calendar as the decision date without testing whether a start could be decoupled from the settlement.

No spousal consult, and there could not be one. The rep nonetheless offered it as an option - 'You have to check the bill, check the books, or talk to the wife, or...?' - twenty minutes after being told the prospect was divorced the previous Thursday, and was corrected.
No fear or doubt objection. The prospect was confident in the approach and in his own ability to execute, having already lost 55 lb unaided.

A genuinely unscripted situation with no play behind it: a prospect whose finances are not merely tight but formally unknowable until a legal process completes. He is not saying no, he is saying he cannot compute an answer, and every scripted money move assumes a knowable financial picture. The right shape here is probably a held start date or a deposit against a start after the settlement, and the script offers nothing. Note also that the prospect rejected the Primal University downsell in favour of the flagship - 'I'd rather be able to figure out the one-on-one. That's what matters' - which is the opposite of the pattern on the other calls in this batch and was not treated as the buying signal it is.

notes: Structurally the strongest sales call in the batch - a properly asked why-now, a real commitment check before presenting, and the best nutrition discovery of the twelve - and it still skipped the Consequence Frame entirely and never touched the prospect's two children or his back surgery. Two hard corrections: never suggest timing a purchase to reduce a divorce settlement, and do not quote tiers that are not on the menu. The follow-up is real and dated, so book the callback rather than waiting to be texted.
